mainTopic: Why the חכמים believe a person who denies two witnesses: self-belief or מיגו, tested through cases of טומאה
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof: one witness is believed about someone's sin as long as the person does not deny it. Then the גמרא turns to the מחלוקת in the משנה. Two witnesses say a person ate חלב, and he says he did not. רבי מאיר obligates him with a קל וחומר, while the חכמים exempt him. The גמרא asks for the חכמים' reason. One possibility is that a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people. The other is a מיגו, since he could have said 'I did it on purpose.' The practical difference is a case of טומאה. Under the מיגו reason, old טומאה is exempt because he could say 'I immersed,' but new טומאה is not. A ברייתא seems to prove the first reason, but רבי אמי reads it as a מיגו. The גמרא then brings a second ברייתא, where the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about חלב and entering the מקדש but not about טומאה. It begins asking what kind of טומאה case that ברייתא means, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be about one witness, so he is believed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא speaks of a single witness and teaches that he is believed when the person does not deny him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא must be talking about one witness. It teaches that when the person does not contradict him, the witness is believed. Learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its proof: the ברייתא is about one witness. So one witness is believed as long as the person does not deny what he says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this line, the גמרא ruled out reading the ברייתא as a case of two witnesses. With that reading gone, the only option left is one witness. That proves a single witness can obligate a person to bring a קרבן חטאת when the person stays silent.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that… (the only reading left)
Contradicts or denies the witness
Is believed or trusted
Learn from this (the proof stands)

steps.whatToRemember: One witness is believed about another person's sin as long as that person does not deny it.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it about one witness,
and it teaches that when he does not contradict him, he is believed?
Learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the proof that the גמרא was building at the end of the previous amud.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A single witness obligates a חטאת when the person does not deny it.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's argument from a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where רבי מאיר argues with a קל וחומר that two witnesses can obligate a person to bring a חטאת even when he denies their testimony.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר said: this follows from a קל וחומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new part of the משנה, רבי מאיר's argument. This line sets up the discussion about the חכמים who disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, two witnesses say a person ate חלב, and he says 'I did not eat.' רבי מאיר reasons that two witnesses can bring someone to the death penalty, which is very severe. So they can surely make him bring a קרבן, which is much lighter. The חכמים answer that he could have said 'I did it on purpose,' and someone who sins on purpose does not bring a קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stricter one (or the reverse)

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir said: It is a קל וחומר.
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting רבי מאיר's line from the משנה. His full argument: if two witnesses can make him liable to death, surely they can make him bring a קרבן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, a quote from the next part of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, two witnesses obligate a חטאת even when the person denies their testimony.

steps.title: Why do the חכמים exempt him?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason of the חכמים is. Is a person simply believed about himself more than a hundred witnesses, or is he believed because of a מיגו?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: what is the reason of the חכמים? Is it because a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people? Or is it because of a מיגו: since he could have said 'I did it on purpose' and been exempt, he is also believed and exempt when he says 'I did not eat'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks an open question about the reason behind the חכמים' ruling and offers two possible answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first option is a broad rule: a person's word about himself beats any number of witnesses. The second option is narrower. He is believed only because he had a better claim available ('I did it on purpose') that would also have exempted him. The answer matters because each reason covers different cases.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)

keyTerms.term: אָדָם נֶאֱמָן עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ
keyTerms.meaning: A person is believed about himself more than a hundred people
Since he could have made a better claim, we believe the claim he did make
On purpose. Someone who sins on purpose does not bring a חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'believed about himself' with the מיגו. The first does not depend on any other claim he could have made. The מיגו works only because the claim 'I did it on purpose' was available to him.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
What is the reason of the Rabbis?
Is it because a person is believed about himself
more than one hundred people?
Or perhaps it is because we say:
since, if he wanted, he could say
'I did it on purpose' and be exempt,
so also when he says 'I did not eat,'
he is believed and exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks into the reason behind the חכמים' answer to רבי מאיר's קל וחומר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the חכמים' reason the broad rule of self-belief, or a מיגו based on the claim 'I did it on purpose'?

steps.title: What difference does it make?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical difference between the two possible reasons.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the practical difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the question matters in practice. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the משנה, both reasons give the same result: he is exempt. So the גמרא wants a case where the two reasons would lead to different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What practical difference comes out of this?

phrases.english: And what is the practical difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks why the question in the previous step matters.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a case where the two reasons would lead to different rulings?

steps.title: The difference shows up in a case of טומאה
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether we can settle a case of טומאה from here. If a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people, it makes no difference whether the witnesses speak of new טומאה or old טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is whether we can settle the case of טומאה from here. If you say the חכמים' reason is that a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people, then there is no difference between new טומאה and old טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference shows up when witnesses say someone was טמא, for example when he entered the מקדש, and he denies it. This step explains only the first reason; the other side comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the first reason, his word about himself wins no matter when the witnesses say he became טמא, today ('new') or at an earlier time ('old'). So he would be believed in both cases. The גמרא is setting up a contrast with the מיגו reason, which may not apply equally to both.

keyTerms.meaning: To settle or resolve a question
New טומאה: the witnesses say he became טמא that same day
Old טומאה: the witnesses say he became טמא at an earlier time
It makes no difference

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a person's broad trust about himself would carry over beyond קרבנות for eating to cases of טומאה, whatever the timing.

phrases.english: To resolve from it the case of ritual impurity,
for if you say the reason of the Rabbis
is because a person is believed about himself
more than one hundred people,
there is no difference whether it is new impurity
and no difference whether it is old impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the practical difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The practical difference is a case of טומאה. With the self-belief reason, he is believed whether the טומאה is new or old.

steps.title: If the reason is מיגו, only old טומאה is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The answer continues. If the חכמים rely on a מיגו, the person is exempt only for old טומאה, because he could have claimed 'I immersed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the חכמים' reason is מיגו, they exempt him only for old טומאה. For new טומאה he is obligated. Why? With old טומאה, he could have said 'I immersed' and been exempt. So even when he says 'I did not become impure,' he is exempt. We can read his words as 'I did not stay impure; I immersed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer about the practical difference. Here it shows what happens if the reason is מיגו: old טומאה is exempt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מיגו means: he could have made a stronger claim that would surely work, so we believe the weaker claim he actually made. With old טומאה, 'I immersed since then' would have exempted him. So his flat denial is read as meaning 'I didn't remain impure.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'Since': we believe his claim because he could have made a better claim and won
Old טומאה: the witnesses say he became impure some time ago
'I immersed' in a מקוה, so I am no longer impure
'I did not remain in my impurity'

phrases.english: But if you say the reason of the Rabbis
is because he can say 'miggo'
the Rabbis exempt him in a case of old impurity
phrases.notes: Exempt from bringing a קרבן for entering the מקדש while impure.

phrases.english: but in a case of new impurity he is obligated.
What is the reason? With old impurity,
since if he wanted, he could say 'I immersed' and be exempt,
so when he says 'I did not become impure,' he is also exempt,
for one can say: what does he mean when he says 'I did not become impure'?
I did not remain in my impurity; rather, I immersed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אָמְרַתְּ טַעְמֵיהוֹן דְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמַר מִיגּוֹ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 5 covered the 'believed more than a hundred' reason. This step gives the other half of the answer: the מיגו reason.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under the מיגו reason, old טומאה is exempt because 'I immersed' was available to him.

steps.title: Under מיגו, new טומאה is obligated
steps.stepSummary: For new טומאה there is no מיגו, because 'I immersed' would not help him. So he would be obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with new טומאה he is obligated. Why? Because even if he said 'I immersed,' he would still be obligated. The witnesses would tell him: you just now became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the מיגו does not work for new טומאה. This finishes the practical difference between the two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מיגו only works if the 'better claim' would really have won. With new טומאה, the witnesses saw him become impure just now, so he had no time to immerse. Without a winning alternative claim, there is no מיגו.

keyTerms.meaning: New טומאה: the witnesses say he became impure just now
He is obligated to bring the קרבן
Just now

steps.whatToRemember: The difference between the two reasons: under 'believed more than a hundred,' old and new טומאה are the same. Under מיגו, only old טומאה is exempt.

phrases.english: But with new impurity, he is obligated.
What is the reason?
Because even if he said 'I immersed,' he would be obligated,
since the witnesses would say to him: you became impure just now.
phrases.notes: In other words, there was no time to immerse, so 'I immersed' could not be true.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the מיגו reasoning from step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Under מיגו, new טומאה is obligated because 'I immersed' is not a possible claim.

steps.title: Proof from a ברייתא that the reason is 'believed more than a hundred'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which reason is right and brings a ברייתא. There the חכמים say 'a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people,' which seems to prove that reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: So which is it? Come and hear: If one witness told him 'you became impure' and he says 'I did not,' he is exempt. You might think the same is true even with two witnesses. רבי מאיר said: it is a קל וחומר. If two witnesses can bring him to the severe punishment of death, can't they bring him to a light קרבן? The חכמים say: a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people. Learn from this that this is the חכמים' reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which reason is correct. It then quotes a ברייתא that seems to answer the question directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states the חכמים' reason in the exact words of the first option, 'believed more than a hundred.' So the גמרא concludes that this, and not מיגו, is their reason. If so, he would be exempt even for new טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: A single witness
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter one

keyTerms.term: אָדָם נֶאֱמָן עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ
keyTerms.meaning: A person is believed about himself more than a hundred people
Learn from this (a proof is being drawn)

phrases.english: What, then? Come and hear:
If one witness said to him: you became impure,
and he says: I did not become impure, he is exempt.
Might you think even with two witnesses?
Rabbi Meir said: it is a kal vachomer:
if two witnesses can bring him to the severe punishment of death,
can't they bring him to a light offering?

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אָדָם נֶאֱמָן עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people.
Learn from this that the Rabbis' reason

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִי: אָדָם נֶאֱמָן עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ.
phrases.english: is because they say: a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting out the difference, the גמרא tries to decide between the two reasons.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים' reason is 'believed about himself more than a hundred,' not מיגו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the חכמים answer רבי מאיר with exactly those words.

steps.title: רבי אמי reads 'believed more than a hundred' as a מיגו
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי rejects the proof. The phrase in the ברייתא is really the result of a מיגו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: Really, the חכמים' reason is מיגו. This is what the ברייתא means: since, if he wanted, he could say 'I did not remain impure' and be exempt, therefore a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי pushes back on the proof from the ברייתא. He keeps the מיגו reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי says 'believed more than a hundred' is not a separate reason. It is the conclusion that comes out of the מיגו. Because he could have claimed 'I immersed,' we end up believing him over the witnesses. So the ברייתא no longer proves the first reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually (keeping the original position)
'And this is what it teaches': rereading the source
Since (the Hebrew form of מיגו)
Therefore

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אמי does not deny the words 'believed more than a hundred.' He reads them as the outcome of the מיגו, not as a separate reason.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: לְעוֹלָם טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said: actually, the Rabbis' reason
is because we say 'miggo,' and this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁאִם רָצָה לוֹמַר: לֹא עָמַדְתִּי בְּטוּמְאָתִי – פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: since if he wanted to say 'I did not remain in my impurity,' he would be exempt,

phrases.aramaic: הִילְכָּךְ אָדָם נֶאֱמָן עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ.
phrases.english: therefore a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי: לְעוֹלָם טַעְמָא דְּרַבָּנַן מִשּׁוּם דְּאָמְרִינַן מִיגּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 8 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The phrase can be read as the result of a מיגו rather than as a separate reason.

steps.title: If so, the טומאה case is the same as the חלב case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי אמי: if the reason is just מיגו, the טומאה case is no different from the case of חלב.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, this is the same as the case of חלב!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי אמי's reading. If he is right, the טומאה case adds nothing new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already taught the case of witnesses saying 'you ate חלב' and him denying it. If the טומאה case works by the same kind of reasoning, it is just a repeat of the חלב case. So why would it need to be taught separately?

keyTerms.meaning: If so
This is the same as
Forbidden fat; the case in the משנה where witnesses say he ate it

phrases.english: If so, this is the same as forbidden fat!
phrases.notes: He means the case in the משנה where witnesses say 'you ate חלב' and he denies it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אמי's מיגו reading from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's claim that the חכמים' reason is מיגו.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is מיגו, the טומאה case would be the same as the חלב case already taught, so teaching it separately adds nothing.

steps.title: Even in impurity he can explain his words: 'I immersed'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא mentions טומאה because you might think a person cannot reframe a denial of טומאה. It teaches that he can, by saying 'I did not remain impure; I immersed.'
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: with חלב, he can explain his denial as 'I didn't eat by mistake, I ate on purpose.' But when they say 'You became impure' and he says 'I didn't,' maybe he can't explain his words. So the ברייתא teaches us that here too he can say: 'I didn't stay impure, I immersed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 10. It explains why the ברייתא bothered to mention טומאה if the reason is only מיגו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With חלב, it is easy to see how he can turn his denial into a story that exempts him ('it was on purpose'). With טומאה, being impure on purpose or by mistake makes no difference, so you might think he has no way out. The ברייתא teaches that he does have one: 'I immersed.' So טומאה is not just a repeat of חלב. It adds a new point about the מיגו.

keyTerms.meaning: He can explain (straighten out) his words, giving his denial a meaning that exempts him
By mistake, unknowingly (the case that requires a קרבן)
On purpose (no חטאת is brought for it)
I immersed (in a מקוה), so I was no longer impure
It teaches us (a new point we would not have known)

steps.confusionAlert: 'I immersed' only helps for טומאה that came before. That is why, back in step 6, the מיגו worked only for old טומאה (טומאה ישנה).

phrases.english: You might have said:
In the case of 'I ate חלב,' he can explain his words:
phrases.notes: This is the case where witnesses say he ate חלב and he denies it. He can give his denial a new meaning.

phrases.english: 'I did not eat unwittingly, but intentionally,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל: נִטְמֵאתָ, וְהוּא אוֹמֵר: לֹא נִטְמֵאתִי,
phrases.english: but when they say 'You became impure,' and he says 'I did not become impure,'
I would say he cannot explain his words,
so it teaches us:
here too he can say:
'I did not remain in my impurity; rather, I immersed.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10 and defends רבי אמי's reading of the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that the extra case teaches something new (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: In טומאה, a denial cannot be turned into an exempting claim, so there would be no מיגו.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even in טומאה he can reframe his denial as 'I immersed,' so the מיגו applies there too, and the case is needed.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: only one who confesses brings the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. From 'והתודה' it learns that only one who admits is obligated. If one witness says he became impure and he denies it, he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he shall confess.' If he admits the matter, he is obligated. If he does not admit, he is exempt. If one witness told him 'You became impure,' and he says 'I did not become impure,' he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new source to help settle what the חכמים's reason is. This first part sets up the ברייתא before the key argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'והתודה' links the קרבן to his own admission. One witness cannot obligate him against his denial. This sets up the next question: what if two witnesses contradict him?

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall confess' (ויקרא 5:5)
Admits the matter
A single witness
Exempt (from bringing the קרבן)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
'And he shall confess' –
if he admits the matter, he is obligated;
if he does not admit the matter, he is exempt.
If one witness said to him: 'You became impure,'
and he says: 'I did not become impure,' he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first ברייתא was deflected by רבי אמי, the גמרא brings a second ברייתא to clarify the חכמים's view.
steps.raayaObject: The reason of the חכמים (מיגו or 'believed about himself')
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, built on the word 'והתודה'

steps.title: Two witnesses: רבי מאיר versus רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks about two witnesses who contradict him. רבי מאיר says two witnesses who could have him killed can surely obligate him in a קרבן. רבי יהודה says a person is believed about himself more than a hundred people.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could it be that he is exempt even when two witnesses contradict him? רבי מאיר said: If two witnesses can bring him to the severe punishment of death, can't they bring him to the lighter punishment of a קרבן? רבי יהודה says: A person is believed about himself more than a hundred men.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with a מחלוקת about two witnesses. The גמרא is still building up to the key line in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר uses a קל וחומר: if two witnesses are strong enough for death, they are strong enough for a קרבן. רבי יהודה disagrees: when the קרבן depends on him, his own word beats any number of witnesses. Notice this is the same phrase from step 8, here said by רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Contradict (his denial)
The severe punishment of death
The lighter consequence of bringing a קרבן
A 'from the stronger case to the weaker' argument (רבי מאיר's reasoning)

phrases.english: Could it be that he is exempt even when two witnesses contradict him?
רבי מאיר said:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֱבִיאוּהוּ שְׁנַיִם לִידֵי מִיתָה חֲמוּרָה,
phrases.english: If two witnesses can bring him to the severe punishment of death,
can they not bring him to the lighter obligation of a קרבן?
רבי יהודה says:

phrases.aramaic: נֶאֱמָן אָדָם עַל עַצְמוֹ יוֹתֵר מִמֵּאָה אִישׁ.
phrases.english: A person is believed about himself more than a hundred men.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא, moving from one witness to two.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה inside the ברייתא

steps.title: The חכמים agree for חלב and entering the מקדש, but not for impurity
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends: the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about חלבים and ביאת מקדש, but about טומאה they do not agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה about forbidden fats and about entering the מקדש, but about impurity they do not agree with him.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the ברייתא. The חכמים believe the person over two witnesses in some cases, but not in a case of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the חכמים simply held 'a person is believed about himself,' they should believe him in every case. They split: he is believed when he denies eating חלב or entering the מקדש, but not when he denies being impure. That split seems to fit the מיגו reasoning, which works only where he has another claim available. The גמרא's analysis of this proof comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: The חכמים agree (in these cases)
Forbidden fats
Entering the מקדש (here, while impure)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up 'ביאת מקדש' and 'טומאה.' In the first, he denies entering the מקדש at all. In the second, he denies being impure.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split between cases is what the גמרא will use to work out which reason the חכמים hold.

phrases.english: And the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה
regarding forbidden fats and regarding entering the מקדש,
but regarding impurity, they do not agree with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא with the line that carries the proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the חכמים's exemption depends on the type of case, which seems to point to מיגו
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא: the חכמים agree for חלבים and ביאת מקדש, but not for טומאה

steps.title: What kind of impurity case is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what exact case of טומאה the ברייתא means, and begins to propose a first answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: What type of impurity case are we dealing with? If we say...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of טומאה case the ברייתא is talking about. This is a setup line: with 'אילימא' it starts a first suggestion, which comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the חכמים do not agree with רבי יהודה about טומאה, but it did not explain the exact case. Before the גמרא can understand that ruling, it needs to know the case. 'אילימא' tells us the first suggestion is coming, and usually the גמרא will find a problem with it.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with? The גמרא's way of asking for the exact situation being discussed
If you say. Opens a first suggestion, which the גמרא often goes on to reject

steps.confusionAlert: 'אילימא' is not the גמרא's final answer. It is a first try, and the גמרא usually shows a problem with it before giving a better answer.
